bullets.title: Fed Hawkish Pivot: Warsh Signals Possible 2026 Hike, Drops Forward Guidance
bullets.body: The June FOMC was uniformly hawkish: rates held at 3.50–3.75% (12-0 vote), but 9 of 18 members penciled in at least one 2026 hike and 5 expect 2+. Core PCE forecast revised up ~0.6pp to 3.3% for 2026; median dot now shows one 2026 hike, one 2027 cut. Warsh stressed 'price stability' 13x vs. labor markets 3x, dropped forward guidance entirely, and shortened the statement from ~340 to ~130 words — markets now pricing 38–40bp of hikes through year-end vs. ~8bp pre-meeting.

bullets.title: Equities Risk-Off Post-FOMC: SPX -1.2%, Mag7 -2.5%, Software -3.1%
bullets.body: SPX fell 1.2% with 85% of stocks finishing lower; NDX -1.0%. Mag7 dropped 2.5% as a source-of-funds trade with Software baskets -3.1%, IT Services -3.6%, and Comms Services -3.0%. Semis were the notable exception, gaining +1.4% led by memory/CPU on persistent AI demand. Citi's post-FOMC sector view: prefer Semis, Capital Goods, AI Power Gen; most exposed short: RTY (small-caps most vulnerable to higher rates).

bullets.title: 2Y Yields +13–15bp on Day; MOVE Index +5% — Rate Vol Regime Shift
bullets.body: 2-year Treasury yields surged 13–15bp to ~4.20% and 10-year rose 4–6bp to ~4.49% following the FOMC. MOVE Index rose 5%, reflecting a meaningful step-up in rate volatility. Warsh's explicit removal of forward guidance means future FOMC meetings will themselves be higher-volatility events.

bullets.title: Warsh Launches Fed Reform Task Forces; Balance Sheet, Inflation Framework Under Review
bullets.body: Warsh announced task forces covering Fed communications, balance sheet ($6.7T), data sources, productivity/jobs, and inflation framework — most to conclude by year-end. He declined to submit his own rate projection. Morgan Stanley maintains its call for Fed on hold through 2026, forecasting core PCE at 3.0% q4/q4, above the Fed's own revised 3.3% estimate.

bullets.title: US-Iran MOU Signed: Oil +1%, Strait of Hormuz Reopening Priced In
bullets.body: WTI and Brent closed up ~1% as the US-Iran MOU approached formal signing Friday. Wolfe Research characterizes the deal as strategically weak for the US — Iran retains Strait control (only suspending tolls 60 days), keeps enriched uranium under IAEA but not US supervision, and asset-unfreezing terms remain ambiguous ($0 vs. $12B claimed). JPM flipped tactically bullish on a potential 'everything rally' but warns it historically fades. IEA cut 2026 global demand forecast 700K bpd and expects 2027 market to move into significant surplus with Strait reopening.

bullets.title: Semis on Parabolic Move; VaR Shock Risk Rising as Market Cap/Revenue Hits 6x
bullets.body: Memory and CPU stocks continued their run post-FOMC, with MRVL +5.5% and WDC +4.4% in Canadian trading. JPM warns semiconductor market cap-to-revenue surpassed 6x (double Mag7), and VaR-sensitive investors (HFs, CTAs, risk-parity) face self-reinforcing selling when volatility spikes. JPM estimates $165B of equity selling from quarter/month-end rebalancing ahead. DRAM/Memory described as on a 'parabolic move with persistent demand.'

bullets.title: AI Chipflation: Apple Raising Prices on Memory Crunch; Policy Levers Being Discussed
bullets.body: Apple is said to be raising product prices due to memory chip supply constraints — a supply-side driven inflation signal with downstream margin implications across the hardware stack. Morgan Stanley's podcast flagged AI memory demand as an emerging inflationary factor and noted policymakers are exploring targeted measures to reduce 'chipflation' pressure. GARMIN noted it built a safety stock buffer; smaller competitors are at risk.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Capex Thesis Strengthens: GOOGL's $50/Watt GPU Deal Signals Higher AI ROIC
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlights GOOGL renting ~110K GB300 GPUs from SpaceX at ~$50/watt annually (vs. implied $14–18 incremental revenue per GW at current GCP/AWS estimates), suggesting materially higher AI monetization products are in development. If GCP/AWS monetize at $25/watt, that implies 27%/16% upside to '27 growth estimates. MS estimates $1T hyperscaler capex in '27 for ~20 GW; META's neocloud opportunity at $25–35/MW adds $4–5+ EPS upside by '28.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Fair Value: ERP Near Median, but Cash Return Ratio at Post-GFC Low
bullets.body: 22V Research notes the implied ERP has risen from 4.35% to 4.6% YTD (near long-term median); naive ERP remains at all-time lows due to high NTM PEs. The S&P 500 cash return ratio hit its lowest level since post-GFC/COVID as incumbent tech pivoted to capex. If cash returns stay depressed 5+ years, fair value is -15% lower; NVDA's $80B buyback and dividend raise from $0.01 to $0.25 are critical positive signals for the buildout cohort.

bullets.title: May Retail Sales Beat: Control Group +0.8% m/m; Consumer Resilient but K-Shaped
bullets.body: Adjusted retail sales (ex-auto) rose +0.8% m/m vs. +0.6% consensus; non-store retailers (e-commerce) up +9.9% y/y adjusted +12.2%. CE/appliances +5.9% y/y. Gas station sales inflated by +42.2% in average gas prices. 2H risks include higher gas prices, moderating wage growth, and higher interest rates; consumer spending expected to remain K-shaped.

bullets.title: Data Center Build Boom: $58B YTD Financing, 850-DC Pipeline Worth ~$7T
bullets.body: Global data center financing volume is up 71% y/y YTD at $58B across 42 transactions. The pipeline stands at ~850 data centers worth approximately $7T. MS estimates a 38GW GenAI power gap through 2028, with crypto mining site conversion offering >14GW of near-term capacity. Texas and New York are pursuing data center development restrictions at county/zoning levels, representing a regulatory headwind.

bullets.title: Power & Utilities: Bernstein Sees 'Once-in-a-Generation' Energy Transition; Bullish CEG, GEV
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated coverage across power/renewables, flagging AI/data center demand, energy security, and decarbonization as structural drivers. Outperform ratings on CEG ($296 PT), GEV ($1,206 PT), VST ($181 PT), NNE ($45 PT); Underperform on FSLR. GEV surged +6.8% and NNE +5.4% on initiation; FSLR -3.6%, ENPH -4.9%.

bullets.title: INTC 18A-P Enters Early Production; Semis Outperform as AI Demand Persists
bullets.body: Intel announced its 18A-P process node entered initial production, meeting timeline expectations and sending INTC +3.5% on the day. The semiconductor complex broadly outperformed (+1.4%) as a sector despite broader equity weakness, with memory and CPU names leading — consistent with the ongoing AI compute demand narrative.

bullets.title: FOMC Removes Easing Bias; Hedgeye Contrarian View: Inflation Peaking, Long Duration
bullets.body: Hedgeye presents the contrarian macro view: inflation is peaking now, crude oil and agricultural commodities are front-running resolution faster than consensus expects, and long-duration/short-commodities is the correct positioning. They note dealer gamma flipped to positive in last five trading days (mechanically suppressing vol), and over 50% of investable capital is rules-based (systematic), amplifying regime shifts.

bullets.title: HOOD Surges 8.8% on SEC Tokenized-Stock Proposal; Exchange/Data Index -3.6%
bullets.body: The SEC proposed allowing tokenized stocks under an innovation exemption, sending HOOD up 8.8% while the S&P Exchanges/Data index fell 3.6% on fears of disruption to traditional exchange revenue (CME -3.5% also pressured by CEO Duffy stepping down early 2027). Investment banks/brokers outperformed the financial sector at +1.9%.

bullets.title: AMZN -3.5% on Reported FTC Lawsuit Risk; META -5.4% on AI Executive Departure
bullets.body: Amazon fell 3.5% on reports of a possible FTC lawsuit over allegedly misleading advertisers, with potential for billions in civil penalties. META dropped 5.4% on the departure of AI executive Emily Dalton Smith. GOOGL fell 2.4% after the UK CMA ordered improvements to search services.

bullets.title: Trump Meets AI CEOs on Global AI Rules; India Trade Deal 'Very Close'
bullets.body: President Trump met with AI CEOs from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and Salesforce to discuss global AI governance frameworks. Separately, Trump indicated a US-India trade deal is 'very close' and plans to ask US companies to manufacture missiles in Europe and Ukraine — geopolitical signals relevant to defense/tech supply chains.

bullets.title: SpaceX Acquires Cursor (Anysphere) for $60B; Full-Stack Enterprise AI Platform Play
bullets.body: SpaceX confirmed a $60B all-stock acquisition of Cursor at ~30x its ~$2B ARR. Moving Cursor inference from Anthropic/OpenAI to Grok could add $500–900M in EBITDA. The deal pairs Cursor's build-deploy layer with Grok and Colossus compute for a full-stack enterprise AI platform (customers include Stripe, NVIDIA, Salesforce). Structural risk: SpaceX's two largest external compute clients (Anthropic ~$45B/yr, Google ~$30B/yr) are cancellable on 90-day notice.

bullets.title: China AI Capex Doubling to $95–151B by 2029; Domestic GPU Share Targeting 50% of AI Capex
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts China AI data center capex expanding from $55–69B (2026) to $95–151B (2029) at 20–30% CAGR, with domestic inference token demand growing 330% CAGR through 2030. Domestic AI chip procurement by cloud providers expected to reach ~50% of total AI capex by 2028. Chinese optical modules/PCB/OSAT players generate 70%+ revenue overseas, capturing global AI compute spend.

bullets.title: June Stress Test (June 24) Could Signal Capital Relief for C, CFG, COF
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises conviction on C, CFG, and COF ahead of the June 24 Fed stress test results. Lower inferred SCBs — C's improved 70bps to 3.6% over two years, COF/CFG tied at 4.5% with improving credit trends — could support buyback capacity and ROTCE targets. Dividend announcements expected in weeks following results.
